$comment: Owner rule R58, runtime proof: user A owns something, user B tries to reach or act on it, the server must answer 403 or 404. Run against the SCRATCH stack (never production): mint two SessionTokens on the scratch DB (afc.settings_scratch), paste them into a LOCAL copy of this file in place of the placeholders, then: node ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs --idor http://127.0.0.1:8010 (the ssh tunnel to the VPS scratch server). The placeholders are never replaced in the committed file: a bearer token in the repo is exactly what R55 forbids.

a.$comment: an ordinary player, owner of a team on the scratch DB

b.$comment: another ordinary player, member of nothing A owns, no admin role

cases.name: B cannot read the Discord reminder settings of an event whose organization B is not part of (events/<id>/discord-reminders/, reopen_event's gate)
B cannot set that event's Discord reminders either
B (no staff role) cannot list deleted accounts (head admin only)
B cannot restore a deleted account (head admin only); an unknown id is 404 and a stranger 403 before that
B cannot set another user's WhatsApp number (admin identity endpoint)
B cannot read the support desk (support staff only)
B cannot invite a co-organizer on an event of an organization B does not own
B cannot rebuild the ranking scores (head admin only)
